source_text.ISS-0932: id: ISS-0932 (queue Q-915, GH-2066); title: D3: Regulatory Compliance Review definition lacks the 21-day timer path to BaFin escalation; severity MAJOR; discovered_by UAT-RUNNER (ISS-0912 QA re-run 2026-10-01). Symptom: POST /instances/:id/advance-timer on risk-evaluation returns 404; regulatory-auto-escalation only reachable from the post-remediation-check unresolved branch. Evidence test/uat-reports/uat-2026-10-01-ISS0912-NARRATIVE.yaml (D3). Scenario test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/meridian/regulatory-compliance-review-bafin.yaml. Definition fixture test/fixtures/qa/meridian_regulatory_compliance_review_process_definition.json. ORCH findings (verify): risk-evaluation is HUMAN_TASK with only {role}; no pending timer exists so advance-timer 404s (Scheduler.resolve_advance_target picks the single pending timer, 400 if >1, 404 if none); edge timeout-risk-evaluation goes risk-evaluation->risk-evaluation-timeout->severity-routing->findings-sign-off, never regulatory-auto-escalation; HUMAN_TASK escalation_timer_duration only reassigns role; a :TIMER node (duration_iso8601) is the engine's routable timer. Required outcome: after evidence-collection completes a pending P21D timer exists, advance-timer fires it, flow runs regulatory-auto-escalation (SERVICE_TASK POST .../compliance/regulatory-notice) -> end-closed, instance COMPLETED; normal path (risk manager completes risk-evaluation -> severity-routing ...) must keep working with no dangling timer trouble. Consider whether reason 'sla_breach_30_days' must be in the service-task body. No QA data/DB changes; repo fixtures/definitions/tests/docs only; bump fixture version if appropriate.

result.summary:
REGISTRY (Step 0.5): docs/issues/ has no resolved entry for this symptom. Related only: ISS-0389 (resolved; built POST /instances/:id/advance-timer, so the endpoint exists and is not the defect), ISS-0912/0897/0930 (seeding; the fixture is already v1.1 from ISS-0930), ISS-0892. Not a recurrence; the 404 is the endpoint working as designed on an instance with zero pending timers.

REPRODUCED (scratch script in the session scratchpad, not in the repo; Transition.transition/3 is pure, no DB): with the current fixture test/fixtures/qa/meridian_regulatory_compliance_review_process_definition.json (v1.1) the graph validates clean (validate_graph, validate_node_attributes, validate_edge_conditions all valid), and BOTH {:escalation_timer_fired,t} and {:complete_task,t} on a token at risk-evaluation move the token to severity-routing and emit no timer event. regulatory-auto-escalation is never reached from risk-evaluation.

ROOT CAUSE (ORCH findings verified, with one correction). The fixture was ported from an R-Co YAML that modelled the 21-day SLA as an out-of-band 'on_timeout' edge convention (edges named timeout-*, YAML comments 'on_timeout for risk-evaluation'); Letflow's engine has no such concept. (1) risk-evaluation has attributes {role: role-risk-manager} only: no escalation_timer_duration/escalation_role, and no :TIMER node exists in the graph, so no timer is ever armed. Transition.dispatch_human_task (lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex:435-451) emits {:escalation_timer_armed,..} only when escalation_timer_duration is a non-empty binary; dispatch_timer_arrival (transition.ex:668-671) is the only other arm path. With zero pending timers Scheduler.resolve_advance_target/3 (lib/letflow/scheduler.ex:348-360) returns {:error,:no_pending_timer} and handle_advance_timer (lib/letflow/routers/instances.ex:726-757) renders Response.not_found = 404 (more than one pending -> 400 ambiguous). (2) Edge timeout-risk-evaluation (risk-evaluation -> risk-evaluation-timeout) is dead decoration: it is unconditioned and declared AFTER e3 (also unconditioned, risk-evaluation -> severity-routing); advance_off_completed_node (transition.ex:538-556) and dispatch_escalation_timer_fired (transition.ex:699-717) both take List.first of the unconditioned/default candidates in declared order, so e3 always wins. The same dead timeout-* edge pattern exists on every HUMAN_TASK in this fixture and in meridian loan-origination (out of scope). (3) regulatory-auto-escalation has exactly one inbound edge, e10 (post-remediation-check, remediation_status=='unresolved'). CORRECTION to ORCH: 'HUMAN_TASK escalation_timer_duration only reassigns role' is wrong. escalation_role is validated by CHK-21 (lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex:905-951, co-required with the duration) but is referenced nowhere else in lib/. When an escalation timer fires, Engine.advance_after_escalation_timer_fired (lib/letflow/engine.ex:2836-2855, persist at 2885+) cancels the pending HUMAN_TASK row (task.cancel audit) and Transition.dispatch_escalation_timer_fired follows the FIRST unconditioned (fallback) outgoing edge of the HUMAN_TASK to ANY target node, skipping every conditioned edge. That is exactly a boundary-timer semantic.

ENGINE FACTS. (a) :TIMER node (transition.ex:638-671; engine.ex prepare_timer_arms 693-754, resolve_timer_arm_attrs 758-779): the token PARKS on the node, arms a 'deadline' timer from duration_iso8601 (CHK-12, graph.ex:839-855), and advances along the outgoing edge only when the timer fires. It is a sequential delay, NOT a boundary event on another node. (b) Cancellation: the only timer cancellation is TaskActivation.cancel_pending_timers/5 (task_activation.ex:505-515), called on instance completion (engine.ex:1965) and cancel_instance (engine.ex:5014); it flips ALL pending timers of the instance. There is NO per-token cancel when a HUMAN_TASK completes normally. Consequence for the escalation-timer approach: after risk-evaluation completes normally the P21D timer stays 'pending' until the instance reaches END or is cancelled, then is cancelled cleanly (normal path inside the UAT/QA window has no dangling-timer problem). If the instance stays open past 21 days the poller fires the stale timer and find_token_for_timer (engine.ex:2609-2614) returns {:error,{:unknown_token_id,_}}, fire_timer rolls back (noisy, latent, pre-existing for every HUMAN_TASK escalation, e.g. swiftroute ops-review PT2H; out of scope). advance-timer during such a stale window would return 500 (render_advance_timer error branch). (c) A parallel split WITHOUT a join is impossible: dispatch_parallel_split (transition.ex:889-941) calls find_matching_join and every branch must resolve to the same PARALLEL_GATEWAY join, else {:error,{:no_matching_join_found,id}} at runtime (static graph validation does NOT catch this). dispatch_end (transition.ex:414-426) completes the instance only when no tokens remain. So a fork of [risk-evaluation chain] and [TIMER -> escalation -> END] cannot race: with a join the join waits for both branches; without one the split errors; a parked TIMER token would keep the instance ACTIVE after the normal path hits END. (d) Graph validation rules that matter: CHK-04 isolated node (observed :isolated_node in the repro when risk-evaluation-timeout is orphaned), CHK-19 (a HUMAN_TASK with a conditioned outgoing edge MUST also have a fallback edge: is_default true or nil/'' condition), CHK-21 (escalation attrs co-required, valid ISO-8601), CHK-17 (CEL syntax). The repro confirmed a condition on a HUMAN_TASK outgoing edge validates clean.

CANDIDATE DEFINITION SHAPES (ranked, lowest risk first). A (RECOMMENDED; zero lib change; verified at Transition level in the repro): make risk-evaluation a HUMAN_TASK with attributes {role: role-risk-manager, escalation_timer_duration: 'P21D', escalation_role: 'role-ceo'}; make e3 (risk-evaluation -> severity-routing) a conditioned edge (variables.highest_severity in none/low/medium/high/critical, same OR-chain style as e6/e7); retarget the existing unconditioned fallback edge timeout-risk-evaluation to regulatory-auto-escalation, and keep it the ONLY unconditioned outgoing edge of risk-evaluation; DELETE node risk-evaluation-timeout and edge e4 (else CHK-04 :isolated_node). Repro results: escalation_timer_fired -> token at regulatory-auto-escalation; complete_task with highest_severity=low -> severity-routing; validate_node_attributes and validate_edge_conditions valid; validate_graph valid once the orphan is removed. Runtime: when evidence-collection completes, the token lands on risk-evaluation and exactly one 'escalation' timer (P21D) is armed (the only pending timer, so advance-timer with no timer_id targets it unambiguously); advance-timer -> fire_timer -> risk-evaluation task cancelled, token -> regulatory-auto-escalation (SERVICE_TASK) -> e5 -> end-closed -> instance COMPLETED (scenario EO-003). Behavior to document: a risk-evaluation completion that does NOT set highest_severity falls to the fallback edge and escalates to BaFin (today it would instead error at severity-routing with no matching edge), so real usage must always supply highest_severity; the scenario's step 2 completes only evidence-collection and step 3 never completes risk-evaluation, so UAT is unaffected. Risk LOW; residual = the stale-timer note in (b). B (NOT recommended): parallel fork after evidence-collection into [risk-evaluation chain] and [TIMER P21D -> regulatory-auto-escalation -> end]; fails per (c). Risk HIGH; would need lib/ engine work (boundary-event node type or END-cancels-siblings) and a decision record. C (NOT recommended): sequential :TIMER node on the happy path; blocks the normal flow for 21 days. D (NOT recommended): change the scenario instead of the definition; contradicts the required outcome.

SERVICE-TASK BODY QUESTION. Scenario EO-002 expects the notice POST to carry reason 'sla_breach_30_days'. The engine supports a SERVICE_TASK attribute 'body_template' (lib/letflow/engine/service_task.ex:226; dispatcher service_task_dispatcher.ex:719/741), so regulatory-auto-escalation can carry body_template with that reason (httpbin.org/anything echoes it, which is how a UAT audit check can observe it). Recommend adding it (low risk, not needed for the 404/path fix). Caveat for the designer: e10 (remediation unresolved) also reaches this node, so a hard-coded 'sla_breach_30_days' would be wrong for that inbound path; consider body_template reading a variable or accept and document. Confirm body_template placeholder rendering rules in the design step.

FILES REFERENCING THE OLD SHAPE / TO UPDATE: (1) test/fixtures/qa/meridian_regulatory_compliance_review_process_definition.json - the real artifact; bump version 1.1 -> 1.2 (seed script creates+activates a newer version and the platform deprecates the prior ACTIVE; a 409 means name+version already exists, so a bump is mandatory) and fix the description ('timer boundary event' wording). (2) test/fixtures/simulation/meridian/process_policy_binding.yaml - named in scripts/seed_meridian_definition.sh as the payload source of truth; keep graph-shape parity (risk-evaluation attrs, e3 condition, timeout-risk-evaluation target, removal of risk-evaluation-timeout and e4, the 'on_timeout' comments); it intentionally keeps relative 'POST /...' endpoints and version 1.0 per ISS-0930. (3) test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/meridian/regulatory-compliance-review-bafin.yaml is byte-identical R-Co port and must not be edited; its step 3 input advance_timer_node: risk-evaluation already matches the new shape. (4) test/fixtures/simulation/meridian/scenarios/regulatory-compliance-review-bafin.yaml and test/letflow/simulation/req208_meridian_test.exs use a test-local @simple_regulatory_review_graph and do not read the fixture; verify unaffected. (5) NEW regression tests, modelled on test/letflow/scripts/seed_swiftroute_definition_test.exs: assert the fixture graph passes Graph validation, risk-evaluation carries escalation_timer_duration P21D + escalation_role, exactly one unconditioned outgoing edge from risk-evaluation targeting regulatory-auto-escalation, no isolated nodes; plus Transition-level pure tests (as in the repro) for complete_task (severity set -> severity-routing) and escalation_timer_fired (-> regulatory-auto-escalation); ideally one DB-backed Scheduler/Engine test that fire_timer on the armed escalation timer drives the instance to COMPLETED with the SERVICE_TASK stubbed as in test/letflow/engine_catalog_service_task_test.exs. test/letflow/scripts/qa_fixture_service_task_endpoints_test.exs globs *_process_definition.json and will cover the edited fixture automatically; test/scripts/persona_actor_seed_drift_test.exs reads the fixture for role names (role-ceo, role-risk-manager already used; re-run it). (6) docs/issues/ISS-0932.yaml status/resolution on close. QA re-seed via scripts/seed_meridian_definition.sh is an ops step after merge, not a repo change.

lib/ AND AUTHZ: NO changes to lib/ or authorization paths are needed for shape A. The advance-timer endpoint and :InstancesAdvanceTimer permission are already wired (lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex:564-565, 998, 1186; lib/letflow/routers/instances.ex:356) and resolve_advance_target already selects the single pending timer regardless of timer_type. Whether the step-3 UAT actor holds :InstancesAdvanceTimer is a persona/authz-grant matter outside this fix (not verified here). Engine changes (per-token timer cancel on HUMAN_TASK completion, a boundary-event node) are separate, larger issues and are not needed. SECURITY-REVIEWER is not triggered (no tenant-data-path code change); REVIEWER and CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR gates still apply per WF-03.

CONSTRAINTS FOR CODE-DESIGNER: fixtures/definitions/tests/docs only; no QA data or DB changes; keep CEL conditions inside the existing grammar (CHK-17); the unset-highest_severity-escalates behavior must be a conscious, documented choice. Not verified here: DB-backed end-to-end fire (Postgres test DB not used per instruction); the shape-A claim is verified at the pure Transition and Graph-validation level plus code reading of the Scheduler/Engine escalation path.

issues.description: Handoff started_at was null on receipt; left null per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL 1.2 (ORCH to follow the two-step dispatch procedure next time).

ORCH premise corrected: HUMAN_TASK escalation_timer_duration does not merely reassign a role; on fire it cancels the task and follows the first unconditioned edge to any target (escalation_role is validated but unused in lib/).

Latent pre-existing engine gap: no per-token timer cancellation when a HUMAN_TASK with an escalation timer completes normally; a stale pending escalation timer errors with unknown_token_id if it fires after the token moved on. Not needed for this fix; consider a separate issue.

result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER: design shape A (escalation_timer_duration P21D + escalation_role role-ceo on risk-evaluation, conditioned e3, retarget timeout-risk-evaluation to regulatory-auto-escalation, delete risk-evaluation-timeout and e4, bump fixture to 1.2, mirror in process_policy_binding.yaml, add fixture contract + Transition tests, optional body_template for reason sla_breach_30_days). No lib/ or authz change.
